analysis: The only change is a one-line addition at head line 1687 of docs/provider/cli-reference.md. It adds a row to the LaunchAgent environment-passthrough table for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES, which maps to DeadlineAdmissionFixes.environmentKey in AdmissionRateEstimators.swift. This is documentation only, with no code, config, or trust-boundary change in the supplied diff. The row sits in the table introduced as the variables `darkbloom start` copies from the invoking shell into the provider plist (LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvKeys + inferencePassthroughEnvKeys). It therefore documents that this tuning variable reaches the daemon. I did not see the Swift source for the variable's semantics or its inclusion in the passthrough list. It appears to be a scheduler/admission-timing tuning knob, so a security effect would be limited to local-operator availability or latency behavior. The operator is already the local owner, and TB-003 treats the operator as having OS-level access. Nothing here touches prompt confidentiality, E2E keys, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041), or the fan helper. The new row also does not weaken the scoping that only affirmative-`1` and listed variables are forwarded. Remaining integration question: if the paired code PR makes the variable change request admission or deadline behavior, confirm that the daemon cannot be induced by non-operator input to bypass admission limits (T-010/T-029 class availability). That code is not in this batch, so I cannot assess it. No finding is raised.
